rows: A honeybee resolves stripes only as fine as about a quarter of a cycle in each degree of view. A person sees more than 200 times finer detail, so the whole picture is very soft.
The two compound eyes together cover about 312 degrees at the horizon. Only a wedge of about 48 degrees straight behind the bee stays blind.

Bees have three kinds of colour receptor, with peaks near 344 nanometres in the ultraviolet, 436 in the blue and 556 in the green. They see ultraviolet light and lose far red, so reds fade and ultraviolet shows as a colour of its own.
bee.jsonl:German Aerospace Center (DLR) and Bee Sensory and Behavioural Ecology Lab 2026
A honeybee can follow flicker up to about 200 times a second in bright light, against about 60 for a person. The picture here steps and lags to hint at how much more the bee catches in each moment.

Phone cameras record almost no ultraviolet, so the app reads bluish and bright surfaces as ultraviolet. How softly the edge of the blind patch fades is also the app's choice, as are the drawing options.
